title: Always been fascinated by this show and was so glad to finally get a ...
transcript: So how do global music icons sting and Shaggy end up in a musical at the Metropolitan Opera? Because this show has actually had a pretty fascinating development process. Originally premiering on Broadway over a decade ago in 2014, it featured an original score by sting and was incredibly personal to him, as it was inspired by his childhood growing up in a tiny ship building town. Now, unfortunately, the show didn't last very long, only running about three months, but it does have a bit of a cult following to it, with many people finally remembering that original Broadway production despite the tepid reviews. And since then, the show has undergone massive revisions over the years, multiple book writers have come in to try and fix it, characters and songs have been cut and added, and now it has finally reached what many assume to be its final form. Sting has come back to reprise his role as Jackie White, a role that he also briefly played on Broadway. And this time he is joined by Shaggy, who plays a character that is completely new to this iteration of the show. He is this enigmatic figure known only as the ferryman. But given what a personal show this is for sting, it is no wonder why he keeps trying to make it work. He describes working on the show as paying a sort of “soul debt,” a way to give back and pay tribute to the community that raised Him, and that he was so desperate to escape
